description: Sclerotinia stem rot is a fungal disease that attacks the stems of many crops. The fungus produces white cotton-like mold and black survival structures called sclerotia. Infected stems become soft, rot, and may cause the plant to collapse.
symptoms: Soft rot on stems near the soil line
White cotton-like fungal growth on stems
Black seed-like sclerotia inside or on infected stems
Plants collapsing due to stem decay
visual_symptoms: black hard sclerotia in infected tissue
disease_cycle: The fungus survives in soil as sclerotia for several years
Sclerotia germinate and form apothecia (cup-like structures)
Apothecia release spores into the air
Spores infect stems or leaves during wet conditions
New sclerotia develop on infected plants and return to the soil
impact: Major yield losses in susceptible crops
biological_control: Use biological agents such as Coniothyrium minitans
Apply beneficial fungi like Trichoderma species
chemical_control: Apply fungicides when environmental conditions favor the disease
Use protective fungicide treatments during high-risk periods
prevention: Monitor crops regularly during cool and wet periods
